reviews.text: Lijiang Old Town (Lìjiāng Gǔchéng) is a famous ancient town in Yunnan Province, China. It’s one of China’s most beautiful and well-preserved old towns, and it’s listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site (since 1997). Lijiang also possesses an ancient water-supply system of great complexity and ingenuity that still functions effectively until now. Today, Lijiang Old Town is full of Boutique Inns, Tea houses, Cafes, and Souvenir shops, and very lively at night with lanterns and music. A mix of traditional culture and tourism. If you like historical towns, culture, and mountain scenery, then Lijiang is very special.

Lijiang Old Town, also known as Dayan Ancient City, is a remarkably well-preserved historic city nestled in the Yunnan Province of China, primarily inhabited by the Naxi ethnic group. UNESCO World Heritage Site: It was inscribed on the UNESCO list in 1997, recognized for its unique urban layout, architecture, and enduring Naxi culture. Unique Features: The town is famous for its intricate network of canals, waterways, and stone bridges, which are fed by the surrounding mountains. The streets are paved with local stone slabs, and the architecture is a distinct blend of Naxi, Han Chinese, and Tibetan styles, featuring traditional timber-framed houses. Cultural Hub: It serves as a living example of the unique Dongba culture of the Naxi people, which includes a rare pictographic script and traditional music. Vibrant Center: The heart of the town is Sifang Street (Square Street), which was historically and remains today a bustling center for commerce and social gathering. Establishment: The town was first built during the Southern Song Dynasty (960–1279) and expanded greatly during the Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties. Trading Post: Its strategic location made it an essential stop along the Ancient Tea Horse Road, connecting Yunnan with Tibet, Sichuan, and Southeast Asia. This function facilitated significant economic and cultural exchange between various ethnic groups, including the Naxi, Han, Tibetan, and Bai. The Mu Clan: For over 500 years, the town was governed by the hereditary chieftains of the Mu clan (Naxi rulers), whose magnificent former residence, Mufu Palace, remains a key attraction. Water System: The town's ingenious and complex water supply system, originating from the Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, was a crucial factor in its design, bringing water to every household and street—a unique feature that has earned it the nickname the "Oriental Venice." Preservation: Despite surviving numerous earthquakes (including a major one in 1996), Lijiang Old Town has largely retained its original Ming and Qing dynasty structure, leading to its global recognition as a cultural treasure. Visited this old town many years ago while making my way through China, and this town was simply a slice out of history, the location, people and experience was magical. We took a donkey ride and a large hike up a mountain.

One of the largest if not the largest old cities with small shops. This place is massive. Best to start at the South Entrance where the food stall markets are and work your way through. There are quite a few TikTok/routine hot stalls, especially the fruit place that makes a decent fruit salad, it's the one with the long line straight down near the food stalls after going through the south entrance, just past an arena where there are lots of skewer shops

I really like exploring the ancient town here, even though I know the buildings are newly renovated and not actually ancient, but the look and feel is there. It’s also super convenient to eat, and things are really cheap (I live in America so cheap is relative). There are unique experiences here that highlight the local culture such as the mushroom hot pot (Lijiang is known for their diverse variety of mushrooms). Because we went during off-peak season it wasn’t overt crowded so it was nice. After dark the lights turn on and there’s street performers (there was even a concert stage performance the day we were there) which is all free to watch.

The LiJiang ancient city is one of the biggest in yunnan province. It has a super unique point, it is the only city without city wall. In ancient China, city wall is the sole protection for the citizens and it separates the city with rural area. Due to the lord of the city family name Mu which in Chinese word is “wood”, he felt that having city wall symbolize putting himself “wood” into a square box, which in Chinese word symbolize “trap”. Thus, he decided not to have city wall. Here the main attraction is the flower displays but I came during winter which is the season with the least flowers. There are many streams around the area flowing into one main stream / river which is connecting the Heilongtan. Vehicle is not allowed in the ancient city compound. Many restaurants and shops. A lot option for guesthouses, many options for live bar too.

The town feels like a step back in time. Cobblestone streets wind through clusters of traditional wooden Naxi-style houses, their dark timber frames and curved tiled roofs reflected in narrow canals. Red lanterns hang outside teahouses, and small bridges arch gracefully over the waterways. A must visit when in China! Also, be sure to visit the traditional costume shops to immerse your cultural experience!
We are staying in the old town so spent lotsa time exploring this place which is a maze. I can see many stores selling the same food items too. Very nice place with many pubs.

Lijiang Ancient Town is always lively, especially at night when the streets are crowded with people, food stalls, and music. It is very commercial, but that also means there’s a wide variety of good food, bars, and cultural shows to enjoy. The town blends a traditional setting with a bustling, modern nightlife atmosphere—an interesting fusion that makes it both vibrant and unique.

Okay to go as a first time visitor, but it’s not somewhere I want to return as it is way too commercialised. The stores are repetitive and full of tourist traps (please avoid shops selling spiritual/wooden beads, bracelets etc), they will use their usual trick (poke the inside of the bead where the string enters to show it is red hence authentic), but it is dyed cheap wood as real wood does not bleed on to the string. Unfortunately we fell for a cny100 bracelet (shop in photo) but after wearing it, noticed the color of the dye stained the white string, and that’s when a bit of research made us realised we were scammed. A quick search online - It can only be sold as cheap beads of cny5-20. Similarly, try to avoid buying too much coffee from the brand “Chuyungu”- you will see it nearly every street in all the tourist old towns and they told us to buy to cny1000 for additional free beans, and the staff that made us the coffee was not knowledgeable at all as he said that there is no difference in ground coffee or whole beans and even ground coffee can keep fresh for many months (which is totally absurd). After buying the beans, one of the staff told us to pay directly to her as their QR code was not working (sounds strange to me). Very unpleasant experience. I had a much better experience at a coffee shop at Baisha old town. Just go for a stroll, eat food you enjoy, buy inexpensive things that are not so prone to scams. It is very vibrant at night.

Lijiang Old Town feels like stepping back in time. Nestled in the mountains of Yunnan, this charming ancient town is a maze of cobblestone streets, wooden houses, red lanterns, and flowing canals. The atmosphere is lively, especially in the evenings when music fills the air and local shops come alive. Walking through the town, I was struck by the blend of Naxi culture and historic Chinese architecture, especially at landmarks like the Mu Residence and the Black Dragon Pool. It's easy to lose track of time here, while exploring the hidden alleys….It’s amazing that the province is able to maintain the old town - as a traveller I get to experience it’s full culture, beauty, and charm..

I recently visited lijiang old town and was pleasantly surprised by how great the overall experience was. The prices were very reasonable, definitely a good bargain for what you get. The environment felt clean, comfortable, and welcoming, making it a nice spot to relax and enjoy your time. Another big plus was how convenient the payment process was. They accept Touch ‘n Go, so paying was quick and easy without any hassle. Overall, I had a really good impression it's affordable, comfortable, and modern. I’d definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for good value and a pleasant atmosphere.

Visited last October — just amazing, no other word for it. The old town has this magical vibe with cobblestone streets, canals, and mountain views that make you feel like you stepped into another world. I even shot my cover of Cry Me a River by JT right there, that’s how inspiring the place was. A must-see if you ever get the chance. 🌄🎶

The Old Town of Lijiang has topped China my bucket list for several years. I was lucky to finally visit it few months ago (in March). The weather was quite chilly, morning temperatures can drop to around 1-2°C. During the day, it stayed below 20. This old town is majorly geared towards tourism, so most of the shops are selling souvenirs, offer traditional clothing rental and photography service. It looks beautiful with all the flowers and lights. The restaurants, bars and hotels are all nicely designed. This town become very bustling and lively at night, especially around the square market. It is surrounded by clusters of bars with live bands and huge dogs around (The doggies are very gentle). Some of the best photo spots includes the water wheel, the sakura restaurant, Nanmen bridge and the hilltop view. I spent around 2 days here as the old town is quite large and full of life. One of the best old town I’ve ever visited!

Huge, pretty, historical, and architecture is just amazing! Super great vibes as well, so lively and happening at night! Took three days to explore the whole area by foot properly. Love this place so much! Views from the top are amazing. So much good food to eat, and sights to explore. 😍 Particularly LOVE taking pics with the tribal costumes! The ladies here are so amazing with their hair and make up skills, transforming me to an ancient princess in an instant hahaha. Had loads of fun and would say this is the main highlight of my Yunnan trip! 🥰👍😊🥰

Its quite big and its so nice to get lost in the alleys, absorbing the cultural sites and sounds around me. Its beautiful for sure and not as crowded as other ancient towns in Dali. Come in the mornings or late afternoons as by 7pm some alleys r packed with people.
The old town is beautiful but can get pretty crowded at night. Almost all of the shops look the same after a while. Best enjoyed at 6am before everything opens.

We enjoyed the vibes here in the Old Town, especially at night. Lots of shoppings and restaurants at the fringe of the old town. Also nice to take photos here with the Jade Dragon Snow Mountain. A short walk is the Black Dragon Pool, a great spot to take the snow mountain during sunrise

Feel free to explore and settle for a cup of locally produced tea before heading towards the bars and clubs for a night of debauchery. It is a good place to stay, while trying to get to nearby tourist sites. The entrance fee was confusing. None was collected from me when I was there. It must be a low season.

Would recommend wearing a good pair of walking shoes as the roads are made of large stones that are sometimes uneven, and can be slippery when wet. It gets really bustling and crowded at night from nightclubs and loud bands, so avoid going at night if you don’t like crowds.

It’s a beautiful place. If you’re expecting full bloom, then must visit during the right season. It’s a happening place. Visited during the later afternoon to avoid the sun and you get to enjoy the night scene when sun sets. There are many entrances/exits to the place. So need to be ware when booking the DiDi cars for pick up.

It’s free to enter. Really interesting place, one of the larger ancients towns with lots of stalls, photo stalls where you can have traditional costumes and make up done in a jiffy for photography. I love the lights and bands playing. Really happening place especially near the weekend. You can get really nice fresh flower cake(biscuits) from RMB 1-3. And deliciously fresh beef skewers for RMB 8 each.

Nestled in the heart of Yunnan province, the ancient town of Lijiang is a place of rare beauty and enduring charm. Recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, it offers a stunning tableau of well-preserved culture, architecture, and ethnic traditions that breathe life into every alley and canal. Strolling through Lijiang’s cobblestone streets feels like slipping through time. Traditional wooden houses line the pathways, their intricate carvings glowing softly beneath rows of red lanterns. Narrow canals thread through the town, their glassy surfaces mirroring bursts of blossoms and sky, adding to the town’s dreamlike aura. The maze-like layout invites curiosity—each turn reveals a quiet courtyard, an artisan’s shop, or a whisper of history. As dusk falls, Lijiang transforms. The town sparkles under the glow of lantern light, and the strains of folk music drift through the night air. Local musicians, perched along the canals, strum ancient melodies that echo through the stone lanes, conjuring a sense of timeless wonder. Though Lijiang Ancient Town attracts travelers from around the globe, its soul remains intact. It’s a rare place where history, nature, and local culture intertwine effortlessly. For those seeking a journey rich in authenticity and beauty, Lijiang promises a deeply memorable experience. If your path leads to Yunnan, let this enchanted town be part of your story.

We stayed at the South Gate (Nan Men) and went to 4 different Qing Zhen / Muslim friendly restaurants in the area. During the night, it was lovely and can be pleasantly quiet off the main streets, with some people having night photography sessions. The old palace of Mufu was relatively peaceful too and a good vantage point for views of the town, without climbing all the way up Lion Hill which charges a fee. Bought flower cakes and a fruit wine, all good.
Very old city with good infrastructure and clean. Beautiful flowers by the roadside and love the smell.

That’s a beautiful traditional Chinese city. I recommend to visit it during the day and night as there are different things to do. Very safe place. December period is best as it is not too cold and it’s outside tourists season. Avoid hotels inside the old city not because they are not good but you may find it difficult to carry your luggage there as it’s going up and down and the roads are not flat. When I was there I stayed at Hotel Indigo Lijiang which is located at the south west entrance of the old city. The hotel was fully renovated, very clean and staff were very helpful and help us organizing our trip to the Dragon Jade Mountain. The first day he offered us tea and we talked for an hour. You can visit the Shizi Mountain from where you’ll see the panorama. They also have beautiful gardens and lots of small traditional shops, rose cakes, tea and coffee. If you love coffee but some beans there as they produce their owns. I recommend staying 2 to 3 nights as it’s enough time visit the old city and the Dragon Jade mountain area.
I love LiJiang GuCheng (Old town), hardly to see white cloud, all are blue skies. People are nice and friendly. Many nice restaurant. Especially we like a restaurant serving nice snow fish.

Visited during low season will be more enjoying bevause you can avoid the crazy crowd. Very nice and clean old town, nice architeture, nice people. BUT beware of the shops selling flower tea. They are scammers and believe all are from a same owner. They will keep talking to you and scope a big bag of flower tea for you, you will only realized how expensive it is when you make payment. Most foreigners cant react too quickly because of foreign currency exchange rate. Luckily LiJiang old town allow 100% refund and pls fully utilize your right if you feel you got scammed. Generally the people are nice but one bad apple can spoil the whole bunch.

It's the most beautiful old town I have ever been to. It's an amazing experience immersing myself in hundreds of years of history. The place is clean and well kept. Strolling down the streets you can find good street food, nice souvenir shops. At night, you must not miss the bars along the main street. Also, don't forget to enjoy the great view of the whole town from up the hill.

丽江古城 Lijiang Old Town is one of the 3 old town in Lijiang. This being the biggest, most central but is also the most commercialized. That being said it is a huge place with all the major tourist attractions points like 大水车 big water wheels, 木府, 黑龙潭 black dragon pool among many others. This is a must visit place in Lijiang. There are also inns and guesthouses in this Old City.
Definitely a great place to walk around. Full of eateries, souvenir shops, cafes, bars. Can easily spend up to 5hrs here.

Ancient hill town reconstructed after the 1996 earthquake. Very pretty. Great tea houses and loads of craft shops, silversmiths and small stores selling snacks and treats. Cobbled streets, canals and scenic bridges. Very friendly people and lots of cultural experiences to enjoy.

The Old Town of Lijiang in Yunnan Province is an absolutely stunning place that is definitely worth a visit. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997 with a special charm thanks to its beautiful timber-framed and tile-roofed buildings as well as to the culture of the Naxi people (an ethnic minority), that amongst others shaped the Old Town. You might get lost, but then you can discover amazing courtyards and romantic little streams around every corner - absolutely gorgeous. I recommend visiting the Old Town during the day as well as evening, because the atmosphere is quite different. (Our hotel was inside the Old Town, which was very convenient). We visited Mufu palace which reminded me of the Forbidden City in Beijing (only smaller) with a beautiful garden where you have a fantastic view over the Old Town and the mountains. Dragon Pool Park, only a short walk from the Old Town, is also really beautiful! Our hotel organized a driver for one day so that we were able to visit the wonderful Jade Dragon Snow Mountain Area (Blue-Moon Valley and Spruce Meadow) and Baisha Village. We stayed for two days, but a little more time would have been perfect…

I am absolutely in love with old town Lijiang, it's beautiful and full of amazing food. If you are planning to go to Lijiang, I will suggest you to stay in a BNB inside the old town so you can enjoy Lijiang's old town view from sunrise to sunset.
Lots of people even on low season. Walk way are nicely light up. But careful with uneven ground made of stone block.

Nice place to wander around. Attracts a lot of tourists, so an abundance of more established chain stores have opened, which is a bit of a pity. There is a night food market at the Southern end of the old town which is interesting to wander around.

A must visit place! I was really impressed with the beauty of the Old Town of Lijiang. The Old Town at night or day has its own beauty. Explore the town at day if you’d love to admire the beauty of quiet time and ancient architecture. To enjoy the hustle and bustle and the culture here, you can visit the town at night. The Old Town of Lijiang comprises three component parts: Dayan Old Town (including the Black Dragon Pond), Baisha and Shuhe housing clusters. Lijiang also possesses an ancient water-supply system of great complexity and ingenuity that still functions effectively today.

The Old Town of Lijiang 丽江古城 is a well preserved UNESCO World Heritage Site founded in the 12th century AD. It is like a fairyland from the centuries past. The city today is teeming with life as tourism blossomed. Highly recommended staying in this old town for a few days to experience its history and diverse cultures.

I have been to Old Town of Lijian on 23 April 2024 in the evening. The weather is chill out. No need to wear any special costume. I tried the local costume with a professional photo grapher about ¥ 200. I got the photo from the shop about 3 days later and could choose 5 pictures for photoshop. This was one of my favorite moment in The local costume. I did not do any shopping as I have bought some local ptoducts from the old towns in Dali and Shanggri-La already.

One of the few memorable places in China where history is well preserved as in the layout, structures of buildings and houses. Traditional houses stand and local customs very much preserved to a large extent. The cobblestone street adds to the ambience of ancient town of Lijiang and best of all, the very old Water Windmill is a major attraction. Stayed in ancient town, 2 times for a couple of days. Worth the money!!!
This is a beautiful old town to visit. A lot of restaurants for choice. Great food, many tourists. Highly recommended ☺️
A beautiful place to walk through during the day. We heard the night life is even better. Tons of bars and restaurants to choose from. Streams of water run along side the buildings.

The Old Town of Lijiang is a beautiful ancient city full of charm and history. The cobblestone streets, traditional houses, and canals create a magical atmosphere, especially at night with all the lights. A must-visit UNESCO World Heritage Site in China.
I do not recommend this place for anyone expecting a genuine old town. The whole place is newly built or renovated, full of Disneyland-style stores.

Beautiful old town of Lijiang. This place is huge! Shops are kind of repeated. Lots of small alleys to be discovered too. Toilet is free of charge, available at multiple locations and most importantly it is clean. Night time has a different feel and less crowded. Do visit the bar street at night for a drink.
Old town is amazing! It looks like a town from a long time ago with so many shops, alley ways, and food! Follow the river and it is romantic and lovely day and night!

I stayed in the old town of Lijiang for a few days and well worth the visit (2012). Plenty of interesting local cultural places and shops to visit. Very toursity so you will not be lonely. In fact it gets a bit crowded but there is a very friendly atmosphere. You need at least 3 days here to experience everything. Great bars and restaurants with a variety of beverages and cuisines.
Huge ancient town, with lots of different alleyways to explore. When I’m here (June 2024) entry fee is no longer required to enter the Ancient city
A beautiful but very touristic area. Lots of souvenir shops and everywhere the same. Visit during calm hours during the day but make pictures at night.
An absolute magical place, recommend time to spend here is two hours but you could spend the whole day soaking in the culture and historic buildings

Ok, I think this place has changed a lot since it was designated as a UNESCO site. It is now dominated by outsiders who have coopted the local buildings to sell things specifically geared towards tourists (hua bing, djembe drums?) and in this sense it is quite frustrating. But it is really wonderful to wander through every street of the old city at different times of day. After a week I think I have fallen in love with the place!

Old town Lijiang was built in such a way as to pamper tourists. The buildings are neatly arranged in an interconnected alleyway, with shades of wood and colored trees adorning the corners, truly a modern old town concept. No wonder so many people come here for pre-wedding photos. At night, Lijiang old town looks sexy with warm, dim colors. We stayed in a small hostel in an alley, really cheap, dusty, but the staffs really nice and the have dogs. Winter season in Lijiang is quite brutal for the tropical gang like us, we need to walk just to make our feet didn’t freeze hahaha. The old city was big. So, if you stopped by the shop beforehand and forgot where it was but wanted to buy, you must have met the same shop on the other side of the road. Like a rabbit milk candy shop — you know a candy they eat with their wrappers, or the fruit stall, or the accessories store, they’re everywhere, in the west, east, south alleys. So don’t you worry about missed out, but get lost.
Beautiful building and construction. Able to see the peak of YuLong mountain with clear sky. Plenty of item to eat, shop and walk around.

The town is beautiful and it keeps and old Chinese style all over the place. It tends to be crowded as its full of shops for tourists but don't expect anyone to speak english ( maybe you are lucky). Overall a great place to visit a couple of days or use a base to Shangrila or any of the natural attractions nearby.

Lijiang is a town that should be on your China itinerary. It's charming and pristinely clean, with lots of great little shops, restaurants and bars, and tourist attractions. The air is clean, the sky is blue, and there are beautiful views from the hills. The nightlife is lively, with lots of live music.

Very clean and unique. Enjoy my staying here. You should find a guesthouse located in Old Town so that you can walk around the Old Town anytime especially to enjoy the night view. I've been here in Dec 2016.

Beautiful old town, like being back in the medieval times. Unfortunately its been turned into a dragonmart with a million shops selling the same stuff. Theres still some amazing little alleyways and hidden gems to look at though, and the hotpot is amazing

I was able to stay in Lijiang for a little under a week in the heart of Old Town. Lijiang's Old Town is an enchanting blend of history and beauty. With its winding cobblestone streets, bridges, and traditional Naxi architecture, the neighborhood feels like a living museum. The town is littered with shops, boasting a diverse array of stores offering souvenirs, textiles, and local delicacies. There are countless dining options where you can savor Yunnan's cuisine while enjoying the picturesque surroundings. Lijiang's Old Town is also a magnet for photographers and tourists alike, making it crowded during most of the day. At night, you’ll see lots of people dressed up in traditional attire for photoshoots. Getting lost in the Old Town streets is part of the adventure and allows for hours of exploration!
Love it… streets are old, stores are new, atmosphere is great… this is a place u need to invest time in digging up the hidden jewels
Clean and fantastic system of waterways and bridges around. However, it's too crowded and noisy, and not as ancient as I expected.

we walked this ancient town over a few days, exploring nooks and crannies, sipping tea in eclectic cafes, and meals in funky restaurants. They call Lijiang the Capital of Amorous Encounters 艳遇之都, lots of single travelers looking for a good time apparently...

A bit of a tourist trap as expected, but there's still plenty to see. Mu's Mansion is worth the price of admission. Sample the local cuisine at slightly inflated prices, but hey, you're paying for the atmosphere, right?

Perhaps due to high season (August), but this was a huge disappointment. Think a mix of Walmart (for the dense crowd) and Disneyland (for the cheesy stuff). The ancient town must have been a great place to visit before they decided to make it a tourist trap. Avoid and focus instead on the mountain and wetlands.
Lovely place. Watch your step because the walkway still remain the taste of old times.
It's still the best old town in lijiang. Particularly the live music and coffee shops up on the hillside.
Lijiang Ancient Town is a living postcard of China's rich heritage, with its ancient architecture, quaint shops, and stunning mountain backdrops painting a picture-perfect scene.
A bit on the touristy side, but still really cool. A surprising amount of variety. Cool little canals.
Lijiang is one of UNESCO world heritage, well persevere architecture from end Song dynasty and early Yuan dynasty. Worth to visit.
A must visit Unesco World Heritage site for any visitor to the town of Lijiang. Can be crowded at all time
Very tourism area. Lots of stores and hostels. All the houses are traditional Yunnan styles.
I feel like falling into ancient period. The building are still in good condition; Mostly converted to accommodation and shops. Learn some Chinese words before are recommend.

Lijiang​ is more than 800 years an ancient city .. Most foreign tourists are more Asian than from Europe .. Lijiang is beautiful in traditional Chinese architecture. Thus, Lijiang was one of the most beautiful world heritage cities in China .. The city of Lijiang is located on the sloping hills of the mountains, making it beautifully, especially when the lights are illuminated at the night .. once in your life you must visit here, worth it.
This old town was really amazing. There is Chinese style building with snow mountain views.

A great place to visit. The street is very big and has many alleys. There are many bustling food and shopping areas. The beautiful scenery here is very wonderful with rivers and streams flowing through the city. My family and I had a great experience here.
Great place. Very colorful and lively spot in the evening too. Must visit if you're in Lijiang.

It is like having night markets, restaurants, bars and bistros, night clubs all in a same area. So many people, so alive; all framed into an ancient city setting of cobblestone streets, water canals and very old buildings. Overwhelming.

Full of character, always a very lovely place, best seen when it's beautiful and serene in the mornings. In the evening it's very lively and noisy with magical mix of traditional music and tasty street food. The houses are lite up at night showing off a mixture of the traditional old build houses and new houses in old style.

Excellent service by 小田and 小杨，the stay here at this tranquil place with super views. Thank you for the wonderful experience. One suggestion will be to have a dedicated area for smokers instead of able to smoke at all common area. Overall a great experience.
Love this old town, people said its commercial but you can find quiet places at South Gate

I loved this place. I had never been to such a unique shopping area. This is probably the most exciting location in the town. If you get lost inside, follow the river upstream to find the entrance. This place is beautiful at night and the local karaoke bars are something you can't miss.

Amazing place with an authentic feeling due to its sheer size. Very relaxing. The flower cakes are a must try in this area. It's also only a short distance to the Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, which itself is easily accessible through a cable car.
Many bar open at this Gucheng and each bar have their own performance. Many street food and restaurants. Night time is better.
Great choice of items on sale. Good food choices. Come here, get lost, spend money, watch your luggage space and enjoy.

Too many shops and restaurants that sell modern goods. And many of them selling similar things. Besides, the road/ path is very narrow compared to other old towns and the volume of visitors. You need to go through many shops and people before you can reach the other spot of interest. A charge of ¥80 per person per day for visitors for maintenance. But no strong enforcement for this fee. No charges for local make it harder to collect the money. Well, for visitors, it's worth to have a look. But you don't need to spend so much time in it unless you have the habit to visit every spot to add into your collection.

A quaint picturesque townscape, full of old architecture and buildings set along narrow streets and alleys. It has a distinct sense of scale and sense of place. A fine place to wander and to discover on foot, the wonderful assemblage of spaces, from arcades to courtyards and squares with a winding canal to boot. Streets are full of activity, day and night with locals and tourists patronising the retail shops and f&b outlets. A wonderful place to linger and enjoy.

A beautiful place that kept traditional Chinese style. The old streets are paved with stones and there is a little stream flowing through the whole town. People are nice, friendly and laid back. It's a place that is good for think and reflection. Unfortunately it is quite commercial as well.

Very beautiful and historic site. Worth visiting for the characteristic local buildings. Once you've been down a few streets you realise that the shops are all selling the same stuff - very touristy - but the buildings are truly beautiful.
Probably the most beautiful township I have visited. A lot of stores for tourists, and at night it really becomes lively. Went here twice as I was so impressed the first time
Obviously the scenery is amazing, but there's not much to do there imo other than sightseeing. There's a palace around iirc but it's nothing you won't see in another Chinese palaces.

Scenic old town with several nice places to go. What is especially annoying about the fee (60¥), is that only Westerners seem to be controlled. On the other hand, the old town is very clean and well maintained.

Place is very "tourist" orientated but worth a look for sure. Prices are not cheap but it costs nothing to look. Had a lovely yoghurt ice cream I'm fairly sure nobody shot into, but there was a fair degree of winking post transaction.

The old town of Lijiang is beautiful, very pretty. The pictures you can take are spectacular if you find the right places. However, the whole place has become a tourist trap: You will lose count of how many tea shops, bracelet shops, silver shops, durian shops and touristic garments shops you'll find while walking in the centre. Seriously appalling if you intend to mingle in the daily life of Lijiang people.
It’s a open air mall. There’s nothing resembling an Ancient Town other than the roofs of the buildings.
Beautiful old town which is maintained surprisingly well. It's definitely worth a visit, but the entrance fee is super annoying. Also the number of tourists is a little bit ridiculous.
nice resort town. Very scenic but a bit crowded with local tourists. Great launch pad for neighbouring areas that are more remote and more interesting.

This is a tourist trap. Almost every building is a shop. Entry requires a really high fee... Basically just so you can shop. To enter the Mu (if I recall the name) Palace, you need to pay a high fee again.

Amazing place full of small details to enchant the visitors. I would put it in my world wide top 10, specially if you also use it as a base for some Yunnan exploration. Better visited during spring, as I can see it getting really crowded during summertime. Life flows gently through its channels, being the one guarded with thousands of bells my favorite one. The 3 main attractions are the old town itself, Mu's Mansion (don't miss it!), and the Black Dragon Pool for the great landscape and vistas of the Yulong Snow Mountain. Shops aplenty, with silver and tea being apparently the main thing here, but I didnt feel confident enough to spend a couple of grands on a teapot. Better get some knowledge before going if you plan to buy fine silverware or old Pu er tea. Guesthouses are everywhere and some are not only beautiful but also well fitted. We stayed at Jun Bo Xuan and do look forward to spend more time there in the future. People in this part of China are not so used to western tourists, so english is not commonly spoken, credit cards are widely NOT accepted (but ATMs are easy to find), and western food is difficult to come by, which is a bummer if you travel with kids. Cars are not allowed in the old town, so prepare to walk a lot. Stop reading this and book a flight to Lijiang!!!
Beautiful ancient town. Hiking, markets, fresh air. It’s not as epic as Zhangjiajie but more romantic!
A must-see on any tour in the area. Very interesting introduction to life and a provincial town in China. People are friendly. Clean and organized. No graffiti.
Amazing place. Lots of shops to buy gifts and restaurants to try great food. If you are ever there, make sure you go to Logu lake. it's by far the best place I visited in China (Logu Lake)
Old city Quarter has individual stalls that sell local products. A good change of atmosphere compared to the shopping complexes with 'international brands'!
Enjoyed the stay. Friendly people and the hospitality included. Well kept heritage site and all surrounds tells of the greatness of care and attention to maintaing history.

The Old Town of Lijiang, which is perfectly adapted to the uneven topography of this key commercial and strategic site, has retained a historic townscape of high quality and authenticity. Its architecture is noteworthy for the blending of elements from several cultures that have come together over many centuries. Lijiang also possesses an ancient water-supply system of great complexity and ingenuity that still functions effectively today.

I loved visiting Lijiang. It was vibrant, historical (despite the fact it's been renovated). You are exposed to lots of Chinese culture. Not a lot of English, so do your research before going perhaps.
Very beautiful place. However, very high prices. Not very crowded in June. Not many European tourist around here. Also, most of the people don't speak English language here.
Beautiful place with beautiful scenery. Places are clean. People are not as bad as it was many years ago. Would come back again.

Lovely historic town with character and flare. Endless food options too with super friendly and accommodating guest houses.
Nice, clean and interesting. But everything is a new constitutions, "the old town" just the name. And entry tickets at the day is expensive.
Plenty of fresh fruits. Shuhe and Baisha are nearby and interesting old places. Good weather.
Lijiang Old Town was inscribed in the World Heritage List due to the fact that the buildings was retained and maintained in features of local ethnic groups, thus preserving historical authenticity
Really lovely old town. I think you'll struggle here if you don't speak mandarin but the city itself is lovely.
in the beginning was surprise with the old town houses. Unfortunately they are not as old as the history as they were re-built after big earthquake.
Ancients town with beautiful scenery, good foods, river and pubs, you will be impressed with the ancients architecture in this town
Most of it is reconstructed, but the atmosphere is still very nice. Definitely worth visiting
Awesome ancient history old town, beautiful street with beautiful buildings, variety of food.
Nice place to visit if you like a bit of Chinese history plus it's very clean and welcoming .
Many shops there feel like market, price also not cheap, anyway the atmosphere is nice.
Quaint, clean, pleasant tourist shopping experience, beautiful flowers, delicious flower cakes.
extremely fantastic and authentic China. Very beautiful mountains nearby and beautiful black dragon garden
Your must go to places when you are in Yunnan. Go try their local Chagee. Walk around and make friend with local
Beautiful cliché, but not local life left, 120% touristy. Except the local market.
Really crowdy too much people there, and the music always the same with percussion.. Just no sense...
Unfortunately very commercial and not representative of a culture gone by. My opinion

Vast area of old town, combined many shop, restaurant, food courts and costume rental shop. You can spend many days in the old town to explore various corners where located bar, silver merchandise, wood scripture, hotel & inn … many famous restaurants among Chinese people located in here also. Visiting the old town at night time is also must-have experience.

麗江大研古城是麗江市的舊城區，連同白沙古鎮與束河古鎮合稱為「麗江古城」，於1997年被聯合國教科文組織列為世界文化遺產，也是3座古城中規模最大的一座，它是中國歷史文化名城中唯一沒有城牆的古鎮，現代流傳的一種說法是因為麗江土司（世襲統治者）姓木，築城勢必如木字加框而成「困」字，所以沒有建造城牆，古城內很多景點都很美，很好拍照！城內很大，要逛完幾個著名景點至少需要3-4個小時，讓停留時間不長的我們感到扼腕！

Thành cổ Lệ Giang, nằm trong 4 đại cổ trấn của Trung Quốc– được UNESCO công nhận là Di sản văn hoá thế giới năm 1997. Nơi được mệnh danh là “Venice của Phương Đông” có tuổi đời hơn 800 năm và là thành cổ duy nhất không có tường thành. Địa điểm sạch, đẹp, người dân hiền lành. Rất nhiều góc đẹp để thưởng ngoạn, check in. Đặc biệt là dòng suối hoa theo mùa len lỏi qua các dãy nhà cổ. Buổi tối khá nhộn nhịp bởi hàng ăn và quán bar. Mình để 4* vì mong có những chỗ hút thuốc tập trung để du khách không hút thuốc tự do ở những chỗ ngồi nghỉ.
麗江，未來之前挺期待的，來了後從下午開始被絢麗的花叢、夜吧一條街、妝造的人們等包圍，基本上看不到原有的色彩.... 唯獨您清晨起個早起、走在稀少人煙古鎮上吃上一碗當地的小吃時，才有真實的看到古都的樣貌。

เป็นเมืองโบราณที่กว้างมากๆ เป็นครั้งแรกเลยที่ต้องเปิด map เพื่อเดินเที่ยวในเมืองโบราณ ร้านค้าที่นี่มักจะประดับตกแต่งด้วยดอกไม้ ทำให้บรรยากาศดูน่ารักแล้วก็เข้าถึงง่าย ในช่วงกลางคืนที่นี่จะเป็นผับกับบาร์ซะเยอะ แต่ในช่วงหัวค่ำก็จะมีกิจกรรมรอบกองไฟ ที่คนท้องถิ่นมาเต้นรอบกองไฟกัน
20年ぶりに訪れた麗江古城はクラブが立ち並び、とても人気の観光スポットになっていました。 面白いのが、お店が閉まると木戸が閉められて昔の街並みに戻ります。それはまるで千と千尋の神隠しの街の様。 新しいものを取り入れて古き良き物を残す、中国の斬新な感覚が面白いです。

Thành cổ Lệ Giang (tiếng Trung: 丽江古城 Lìjiāng Gǔchéng), còn gọi là Phố cổ Lệ Giang hay Old Town of Lijiang, là một trong những khu trung tâm lịch sử được bảo tồn tốt nhất ở Trung Quốc và được UNESCO công nhận là Di sản Thế giới từ năm 1997 do giá trị văn hóa – kiến trúc độc đáo của nó. Được xây dựng từ cuối thế kỷ 13 (thời Nguyên) và phát triển mạnh mẽ dưới thời Minh – Thanh, tổng cộng hơn 800 năm lịch sử. Thành phố Lệ Giang, tỉnh Vân Nam, Trung Quốc, trên cao nguyên ở độ cao khoảng 2.416 m so với mực nước biển. Một trong những điểm nổi bật nhất là hệ thống cấp nước cổ xưa – những con kênh và mương nước chảy xuyên suốt thị trấn, đưa nước ngọt từ các nguồn núi về trải đều đến từng gia đình. Hệ thống này là một kiệt tác kỹ thuật cổ đại vẫn còn hoạt động hiệu quả. ￼ Có hơn 300 cầu đá – gỗ bắc qua các con kênh, khiến người ta ví nơi này như “Venice của phương Đông”. ￼ Đường phố lát đá đỏ (Wuhua Stone) rất bền và không bùn trong mùa mưa. ￼ Khu phố cổ không có thành lũy bao quanh, nhưng tận dụng địa hình núi non tự nhiên để bảo vệ. Các ngôi nhà chủ yếu là cấu trúc khung gỗ – hai tầng, mái ngói uốn cong, pha trộn yếu tố kiến trúc của: • Dân tộc Naxi (bản địa), • Người Hán, Bạch, Tạng, tạo nên sự đa dạng văn hóa độc đáo. 🏙️ Khu vực chính trong Thành cổ Lệ Giang 1. Dayan Ancient Town – Trọng tâm của khu cổ, với quảng trường Sifang và nhiều tuyến đường thương mại cổ. ￼ 2. Baisha Residential Complex – Khu định cư lịch sử sớm nhất, nổi tiếng với tranh tường hơn 40 bức từ thế kỷ 13 thể hiện đời sống tinh thần và tín ngưỡng. ￼ 3. Shuhe Ancient Town – Một phần trạm dừng quan trọng trên con đường Trà – Ngựa cổ (Ancient Tea Horse Road), phản ánh nền thương mại sớm. 📜 Lịch sử & Giá trị văn hóa • Ban đầu là trung tâm thương mại trên tuyến Trà – Ngựa cổ nối Trung Quốc với Tây Tạng và Miến Điện, giúp Lệ Giang trở thành điểm giao thương trọng yếu từ thế kỷ 12. ￼ • Khu phố cổ chứng kiến sự giao lưu văn hóa giữa các dân tộc Naxi, Hán, Tạng, Bạch, thể hiện rõ trong kiến trúc, phong tục, âm nhạc và nghệ thuật trang trí. ￼ • UNESCO đánh giá đây là một “ví dụ xuất sắc cho sự hòa hợp giữa con người và thiên nhiên” nhờ tích hợp địa hình, sông nước và kiến trúc đô thị. 🎎 Văn hóa bản địa • Dongba – tôn giáo cổ truyền của Naxi với chữ viết cổ độc đáo được trưng bày trong nhiều nơi. ￼ • Âm nhạc truyền thống Naxi – một trong những loại hình âm nhạc dân gian lâu đời nhất còn được biểu diễn trong khu phố cổ. Thành cổ Lệ Giang không chỉ là một di sản kiến trúc lịch sử Trung Quốc mà còn là một biểu tượng sống động của sự hòa hợp văn hóa, kỹ thuật cổ xưa và đời sống đô thị độc đáo. Đây là điểm đến quan trọng đối với những ai quan tâm đến lịch sử, văn hóa bản địa và kiến trúc truyền thống Trung Quốc.

2025.10.25 歷史上的今天 我來麗江古城 這是一個特別有底蘊的古老城市 雖然已經很商業化 但是還是很值得來走一走 整個麗江古城是沒有城門跟城門樓的。 因為在麗江古城最偉大的人稱為東巴。他是能夠上之天文下之地理能掐會算。 這位偉大的東巴姓木 他認為如果把麗江古城蓋了城牆，就相當把他的這個木圍起來 就成了一個「困」字 所以麗江古城自古以來就沒有城牆 這是來到這裡之後聽到一個很有底蘊的說法 聽了自古以來茶馬古道的辛苦 還有歷史長河所留下來的故事 感嘆有這樣子的美好 都是值得人們去細細感受 小橋流水 花朵扶疏 歷史的影子從來沒有遠離過⋯ 全留在了城牆瓦片裡⋯

Phố cổ rất đẹp, người đi thăm quan du lịch rất đông. Thị trấn có lịch sử hơn 1.000 năm và đã từng là nơi hợp lưu buôn bán dọc theo đường mòn Trà mã đạo, con đường được biết đến như là "Con đường tơ lụa Tây Nam". Thị trấn cổ Đại Nghiên nổi tiếng với hệ thống đường thủy và cây cầu được bố trí có trật tự. Nền văn hóa ở đây là sự kết hợp giữa văn hóa của người Nạp Tây với các yếu tố trái ngược của những thương nhân người Hán định cư ở khu vực này từ nhiều thế kỷ trước. Người Nạp Tây đã sống trong những ngôi nhà bằng gỗ và gạch bùn mà họ học được từ các thương nhân Nam Kinh. Thợ mộc địa phương xây dựng các khung nhà gỗ công phu theo trí nhớ mà không cần phải có bất kỳ bản thiết kế hay sơ đồ nào khác. Những ngôi nhà này thường được tô điểm bởi các chi tiết chạm khắc hoa văn và chim chóc trên cửa sổ. Các chạm khắc hiện được thực hiện bởi các nghệ nhân dân tộc Bạch, nhưng sự chú ý được dành cho việc mô tả hệ động thực vật bốn mùa theo truyền thống của người Hán. Ngay cả các gia đình nông nghiệp nghèo khó cũng thu thập những gì họ có được để lắp các cửa sổ chạm khắc tỉ mỉ, và dường như coi chúng quan trọng hơn đồ nội thất cho ngôi nhà.
麗江古城於1997年被聯合國教科文組織列入「世界文化遺產名錄」，以整座古城申報世界文化遺產之一。 麗江古城是中國歷史文化名城中唯一沒有城牆的古鎮，建築依山傍水，順水入城，逆水出城。

Lệ Giang không chỉ là những mái ngói rêu phong hay những con kênh thơ mộng mà bạn thường thấy trên ảnh. Với một người du lịch trải nghiệm, Lệ Giang mở ra một thế giới nơi bạn có thể thực sự "sống" chậm lại và cảm nhận. Điểm cuốn hút nhất chính là lạc mình vào mê cung những con hẻm lát đá cuội, hai bên là những ngôi nhà gỗ cổ kính của người Naxi với kết cấu "Tam phường nhất chiếu bích" (ba dãy nhà hướng về một khoảng sân và một bức tường trắng). Những cây cầu đá cong cong bắc qua dòng kênh uốn lượn, tiếng nước chảy róc rách và những chiếc đèn lồng đỏ treo cao tạo nên một bức tranh yên bình, đặc biệt là vào sáng sớm hoặc chiều muộn khi du khách thưa dần.
晚上由飯店叫車到獅子山夜市，地方不太大。 麗江古城夜色美！ 早上到古城中的天地院，感受納西傳統建築及歴史文化。 再登上獅子山上的萬古樓，由上而下飽覽麗江古城景色。

여강고성(V6CP+P8H,Gucheng District,Lij8ang,Yunnan,China)은 윈난성 북쪽 리장시의 나시족이 건설한 800년 송원대 역사를 고스란히 간직하고 있는 올드타운으로 세계문화유산으로 등재되어 있다. 청기와 목조주택 돌로된 옛골목과 거리 주점 4km에 이르는 수로등이 박제된 듯 그대로 남아있다.년중 무휴 24시간 무료 입장이다. 고성하면 떠오르는게 성문과 성벽인데 여강고성은 성문이나 성벽이 없다. 왕국이나 도읍지가 아니었고 순수하게 나시족들이 모여 살던 삶의 현장이였기 때문이다.고성에 들어서면 물레방아와 다리 세계문화유산기념 벽이 보인다. 기념벽을 따라 4단 골목 끝 제일 높은 곳에 오르면 여강 고성을 한눈에 내려다 볼 수 있다. 혹자는 그 곳의 No1 C.2층 까페가 최고라고 하지만 거긴 커피 까페고 좀 더 깊은 여강고성을 음미하고 싶다면 그 주변 찻집에 가는 것을 강추한다. 이제 됬다고 할 때까지 중탕을 해주며 2~3시간을 앉아 있어도 나가라고 히지 않으니 느긋하게 앉아 여강 고성을 즐기는 데 제격이다.마침 투숙한 호텔이 여강 고성에서 500m거리에 있어 밤에 3일 연속 그 찻집에 가서 여강 고성 야경 투어를 즐기는 호사를 누렸다.여강고성은 언제가도 사람들 특히 젊은이들로 넘쳐나며 물레방아 옆 사랑의 자물쇠 하우스는 연인들이 줄지어 사랑의 언약식을 하는 고성의 명소이며 웨딩 촬영의 메카가 되었다. UNESCO세계문화유산으로 등재된 여강고성의 화려함 이면에 극단적으로 흐르고 있는 상업화의 현실은 많은 생각이 들게 만들었다.

第一次到雲南旅遊，麗江古城是行前計畫中的一個重要行程。從我們入住的大理洱海旁旅店到麗江古城，約需兩小時的車程時間。我們到麗江縣是先入住在麗江束河古鎮的旅店，並在隔天先前往玉龍雪山旅遊。接著在玉龍雪山旅遊的隔天，前往麗江古城旅遊。在大理旅店業者的建議下，我們到達麗江古城後，先參觀木府。在參觀木府時，有專門的木府景區解說員，詳細說明木府的歷史文化與環境背景，解說員有條不紊的解說，令人讚嘆！專業度令人印象深刻。接著，旅店業者建議遊獅子山。因為業者說，從獅子山頂可俯瞰整座麗江古城，非常壯觀美麗。但考慮從木府走到獅子山頂的路程較遠且秏時，嚴重壓縮參觀麗江古城其它地方的時間，所以我們並沒有上獅子山頂，而是直接從木府往其它麗江古城景區旅遊。麗江古城是一個沒有(石)城牆的古城，已列入世界文化遺產名錄，光是這樣的名聲，就讓麗江古城成為到雲南旅遊必到的景區。如同大理古城，麗江古城一樣有很大的旅遊範圍，除了古城內的造景，古色古香，美侖美奐外，商業氣息也是頂盛，即使是平日時間，遊客還是超多。而有些遊客是因為，古代大旅遊家徐霞客曾在此長住一段時間，而慕名來麗江古城追思徐霞客的風采。在麗江古城內有徐霞客紀念館，而在參觀古城的行徑上，也有徐霞客的塑像。要好好逛麗江古城，如果加入木府與獅子山頂景區，最好規畫二日遊！才不會逛的零零落落。作為雲南旅遊的熱門景點，麗江古城絕對是值得一遊再遊的地方。

観光地としてはいいかもしれませんが、もはや世界文化遺産と呼べるような街ではありません。 多くの古建築は取り壊され、古建築風の派手な店舗が並んでいます。二階部分がガラス張りであったり、柱にペンキを塗ってあたかも石造りであるかのように見せるのは、とても古城の歴史を尊重しているとは思えません。建築のガイドラインがあるはずですが、全く順守されていないのでしょうか？UNESCOは人類の遺産を守ることに失敗しました。次回監査での登録消去が妥当でしょう。 古建築に興味がある人は、ぜひ他の街を訪れることを薦めます。中国には、よく保存された古鎮が多くあります。 古城の歴史や文化に興味など無く、伝統衣装"風"の服を着て自らに酔いしれ、バーで騒ぎたい人が、麗江を訪れれば良いと思います。

●《麗江古城》位於【雲南省麗江市】大研古城的獅子山腳下，海拔高度約2400m，1997年12月4日被「聯合國教科文組織」列為〝世界文化遺產〞。《麗江古城》又名大研鎮，坐落在麗江壩中部，是一座沒有城牆的古城，據說是因為【麗江】世襲統治者姓“木”，築起城牆就像“木”字加框而成「困」字一樣。古城內木樓青瓦，古街石巷，小橋流水，站在古城東大街上，舉頭即可遙望《玉龍雪山》。 ●《麗江古城》依山而建，街巷依水流而設，古城的標誌是〝大小水車〞，一到古城就能看到一大一小兩個水車，有人說是情人車，也是母子車，水車是古代為人們提供動力的地方，可以協助人們提水灌溉、舂米磨面；如今的〝大小水車〞仍然可以轉動，成了《麗江古城》的一道風景線，是最佳的打卡點。《四方街》是古城的中心，也是“茶馬古道”的交易市場所在。從《四方街》延伸出《光義街》、《七一街》、《五一街》和《新華街》四條主幹道，四條路又衍生出縱橫交錯的街巷，構成了今天以《四方街》為中心的《麗江古城》。 ■《麗江古城》你可以臨河漫遊，跟著水流逛古城：古城充分利用泉水之便，玉河水在城中一分為三，三分成九，再分成無數條水渠，形成主街傍河、小巷臨渠的局面，使得古城清淨而充滿生機；你也可以走街入院，感受『納西民族』建築的內涵：古城建築為古樸的「納西」院落，白牆青瓦木簷，構造粗獷簡樸，而庭院佈置和房屋細部裝飾豐富而細膩，「納西」人民喜歡在院中種植花木，形成人與自然的美好和諧；你更可以穿著拖鞋，坐在四方街上，與曬太陽的「納西」老太聊聊天，感受當地人的生活節奏；而夜幕降臨，喧鬧的〝酒吧街〞是你感受【麗江】夜生活的不二之選。 ●《麗江古城》從當年“茶馬古道”上的重要交易之處，如今延續著一貫的繁榮；古城裡遍佈經營各地特產的店舖，你可以隨意挑選你喜歡的：民族飾品、茶葉、銀器、銅器、東巴紙、披肩…等。逛累了，也無須擔心，古城裡有眾多餐館，無論是【雲南】地道風味美食，還是西餐披薩，都能讓你大飽口福。

리장고성 만의 특유의 고즈넉함과 아기자기한 맛이 있습니다. 하지만 관광객들이 많아져서 그런지 관광도시로 이미 변해버린것 같아요. 한국으로 치자면.... 인사동 같은?? 실제 주거하는 곳이란 느낌보다는 전부다 가게로 채워져 있는 듯 했어요. 하지만 여기만의 매력이 있어요. 길은 돌길이어서 비가 오면 미끄러질수 있으니 조심해야해요. 수로 따라서 길이 예쁘게 꾸며져 있어서 전통복장 입고 사진 찍기 좋아요. 물가는관광지다 보니 전혀 싸지 않아요 한국 관광지보단 싸지만 번화가 물가? 정도 생각하면 됩니다. 커피도 한국이랑 거의 똑같아요 안싸요 ㅠㅠ 메인 수로 거리에 있는 식당은 둘이서 훠궈 먹으니 400위안 ㅎㅎ (7만원 정도?) 강남 물가보다도 비싸요 고성 내에서 이것저것 사먹고 식사할거면 돈 넉넉히 들고 가셔야 해요. 한번은 꼭 가볼만한 곳이예요!
非常大的古城，結合現代與古代的感受，前半段過於商業化，晚上還有PUB, 後半段古色古香的客棧多，部分客棧有很好的視野與安靜的環境，天氣好可以看到月亮，若不是住客，二樓陽台也可收費看景，城內只有電動車，幾乎都需步行，若行李過多或太重，建議不要住在太裡面的客棧，城內有木府園區，需要收費，但是個非常值得細細品味的好地方。

리장고성, 중국인들의 신혼여행지로 인기있는곳 여기저기에서 온 관광객들로 사람들이 넘처난다, 낮에는 관광객으로 넘치고 밤엔 젊은이들의 나이트클럽에서 요동치는 소리로 좀 시끄럽기도하다, 하지만 볼것도 즐길것도 많은곳이다. 기간을 두고 둘러보면 아기자기하게 이쁘게 꾸며진집들과 정원들그리고 옛 고풍스런 풍경들을 감상할수있다, 이곳에서 몇일 묵으며 쉬어가는것도 좋은 생각일듯하다. 생각보다 안전하고 특이한 물품을 구매 할수도 있으며 음식과 술도 대부분 맛이있다. 이곳을 기본으로해서 근처 여행사들을 찾아서 리장 주변의 가볼만한곳의 트레킹 코스도 아니면 하루투어 이틀투어 등등을 해볼수있다. 북쪽의 상그릴라투어, 그옆의 설산투어, 다리투어,호도협트레킹등 여행사마다 단가가 다르니 발품팔이를 해야한다. 꼭!!!

我住在城外的客棧，房東很好客，人很好，很熱情。 古城維護費用80元。作為一個遊客，我只是來參觀，消費，刺激經濟。我沒有破壞古城什麼，也不是在內營商，為何要遊客支付維護費用? 感覺就如付款進入一個大型商場，想吸引更多遊客前來消費，應該自行改善景點配套吧?基本概念上，本未倒置。結果，我倆口子給了此維護費用共160大元，當作是捐獻吧，完全沒有回報，結果，消費意欲大減，古城內及古城外，感覺也沒差，店舖也是差不多，沒多大特色，感覺走十分鐘和走兩小時也是看相同東西。城內所有景點亦要另外收費，飲食消費像極樂園，貴得嚇人。 結論，古城出入口很多，只有走偏一點，不難找到不用捐獻的入口，還有查票人員晚上7至8時就會離開，此時也是古城最美最熱鬧的時候。不明白我為何作出了捐獻，及捐獻了給誰人，誰人作出了貢獻及改善。 我絕對不會再來了古城，亦不會建議朋友進入古城。
瓦屋根の建物が並び、古城の中は水が流れ緑が多く、綺麗に整備されていて、公衆トイレがあり、思いの外きれいでした。ナシ族の衣装をまとった女性をみかけました。夜はライトアップされた古城を歩いていると、あちらこちらのお店から、ミュージシャンの歌声が聞こえてきます。
來過兩次。古城開發的早，除了老房子的美，其他都已不是在地人。一片外來掏金客。店鋪出租外來客，房子出租變民宿。物價已炒作到匪夷所思。只有貴貴貴形容。不過拍照真美。

리장[麗江; 여강]을 끼고 위룽쉐산[玉龍雪山; 옥룡설산] 밑 해발 2,400m에 있다. 면적은 3.8㎢이다. 고원 계절풍 날씨로 여름에는 너무 덥지 않고 겨울에는 많이 춥지 않다. 일년 평균기온은 12.6도다. 일년 강우량은 950mm이다. 리장고대마을의 지리적 위치는 독특하다. 산과 주변의 자연환경을 이용해서 서북의 차가운 바람을 피하고 동남쪽의 빛을 충분히 받을 수 있다. 마을 북쪽의 샹산(象山; 상산) 아래에서 강물이 3개로 나누어져 마을 안으로 흘러 들어온다. 이 강물은 마을 전체로 흘러 들어 모든 집 앞에 강물이 흐른다. 이곳에 사는 나시(納西)족은 3갈래의 강물을 가장 윗줄기는 마시는 물로, 중간에 있는 줄기는 밥하는 물로, 가장 아래에 있는 줄기는 빨랫물로 사용한다. 마을에는 총 300여 개 돌로 만든 다리가 있다. 다리, 강물, 초록색의 나무, 오래 된 거리와 오래 된 집들이 어우러지며 아름다운 마을 풍경을 구성하고 있어 '동방의 베니스(Venice)'라고 불린다. 마을의 중심인 시팡지에[四方街; 사방가]는 명청(明淸)시대부터 서북의 차 상업무역의 요점이었다. 시팡지에의 길 바닥은 붉은색의 우화슬[五花石]로 되어 있어 비가 와도 발에 흙을 묻지 않고 돌의 무늬로 인해 거리의 아름다움이 더 돋보인다. 마을의 건물은 한족(漢族), 장족(藏族), 바이족[白族] 등 여러 민족의 민속을 융합한 나시족의 독특한 양식으로 형성되었다. 1997년에 유네스코 선정 세계문화유산으로 등록되었다.

麗江古鎮始建於宋末元初，至今已有八百多年的歷史。當時麗江木氏先祖將統治中心由白沙遷至現獅子山。西元1253年，蒙古軍南征，木氏先祖阿宗阿良迎降。1254年，蒙古設三賧管民官。1277年，改麗江路通安州。1382年（明洪武十五年）通安州知州阿甲阿得歸順明朝，改設麗江軍民府，賜阿甲阿得木姓，封世襲知府。
Bạn nên đến thành phố cổ này một lần cho biết. Lệ Giang đến giờ vẫn “đặc quánh” không khí cổ kính, toát ra không chỉ từ những ngôi nhà, con phố, dòng kênh mà còn từ phong cách sống của cư dân.

丽江古城始建于宋末元初（13世纪后期）。古城名称来源据说是因为丽江世袭统治者姓木，筑城势必如木字加框而成“困”字之故。丽江古城的纳西名称叫“巩本知”，“巩本”为仓廪，“知”即集市，丽江古城曾是仓廪集散之地。明洪武十六年（1383年），木得在狮子山麓兴建建“丽江军民府衙署”。曾遍游云南的明代地理学家徐霞客，在《滇游日记》中描述当时丽江城“民房群落，瓦屋栉比”，明末古城居民达千余户，城镇营建已颇具规模。清雍正二年（1724年），第一任丽江流官知府杨馝到任后，在古城东北面的金虹山下新建流官知府衙门、兵营、教授署、训导署等，并环绕这些官府建筑群修筑城墙。 丽江古城内的街道依山傍水修建，以红色角砾岩铺就，有四方街、木府、五凤楼、丽江古城大水车、白沙民居建筑群、 束河民居建筑群等景点。如今，丽江古城内商业气息浓重，商贩云集，客栈、酒店、饭馆、小吃店遍布大街小巷，各类旅游商品、纪念品琳琅满目，已经成为国内著名的旅游热点。
